A rolling beverage cooler from Backyard Discovery that holds 100 quarts, built on an acacia wood frame. Acacia is naturally water-resistant, which is what makes the cart suitable for staying out in all weather. Towel racks and a bottle opener are attached to the frame, and a waterproof cover comes with it for the stretch of the year the cart is not in use.

Fourteen by twelve is the size at which a pergola stops shading a table and starts defining an outdoor room. This Stratford covers that span in fully powder-coated galvanized steel finished in white, with posts, beams, and rafters proportioned after traditional architecture.
Range builds the frame from material up to 30% thicker than typical mass-produced options and uses part profiles three times larger than standard small-footprint kits, then tests components for long-term durability in demanding conditions including high winds and coastal environments. The white finish reflects rather than absorbs light, which keeps the space underneath from reading as dim on a bright day.

column3:
Part size is what separates the Stratford from a flat-pack pergola, and it shows most at 16x12. The profiles are three times larger than those used in standard small-footprint kits, and the steel itself runs up to 30% thicker than typical mass-produced options, so a span this wide keeps the proportions of traditional architecture instead of thinning out.
The frame is galvanized steel under a full powder coat in black. Components are tested for long-term durability and reliable performance in harsh conditions, including high winds and coastal environments.

column3:
A pergola this size changes how a house meets its yard, and the Stratford is designed to read as an extension of the building rather than an object dropped into the garden. The 16x12 span in white powder-coated galvanized steel makes a clean transition from indoor rooms to outdoor ones.
Posts, beams, and rafters follow traditional architectural proportions and are cut from material up to 30% thicker than typical mass-produced options, with part profiles three times larger than standard small-footprint kits. Testing covers long-term durability and reliable performance in harsh conditions, high winds and coastal environments included.

column3:
Four to six chickens fit in the Sweetwater, an elevated cedar coop whose 24 sq. ft. run extends underneath the raised floor so the footprint does double duty. Birds get room to scratch and move without taking up more of the yard.
A solar-powered door opens and closes on a timer you set, which shuts the flock in against predators overnight and lets them out in the morning without anyone walking outside. Nesting boxes give hens a quiet place to lay and keep egg collection simple. Roosting bars inside give them a natural perch after dark. Windows bring daylight into the coop and the full front door locks, opening wide for cleaning and daily care. The finish is cedar in a modern white stain under a black galvanized steel roof.

column3:
Brown-stained cedar and a powder-coated galvanized steel roof give this Sweetwater its farmhouse look, but the details inside are what make it workable day to day. It houses four to six chickens, with a 24 sq. ft. run extending under the elevated coop.
The two-hole nesting box gives hens separate, quiet spaces to lay, and a side-access door opens for full visibility into both boxes at collection time. Two interior roosting bars provide 4.5 linear feet of perch, enough for birds to spread out overnight. A solar-powered door opens and closes on a timer you set, closing the flock in against predators at night and letting them out on schedule each morning. Windows let natural light in, and the full front door locks and opens wide for cleaning.

column3:
Sweetwater Heights sits up on a raised deck that wraps around the playhouse, which is what separates it from a ground-level house of similar size. Kids climb the wide step ladder, built with wide-rung steps that suit a range of ages, and take the wave slide back down.
Inside, the play kitchen has a toy stovetop, a built-in sink, battery-powered appliances, and other accessories. A working door and large windows bring in sunlight and fresh air while leaving you a clear view of what is happening from the yard. A measurement board is attached for tracking how much everyone has grown. The space beneath the deck can hold a sandbox or serve as toy storage. Cedar construction in neutral colors keeps the footprint modest for smaller yards.

column3:
The Sweetwater Playhouse is cedar, finished light brown with black trim. A working half door makes the entrance, large windows let in light and moving air, and the snack bar window turns the place into a cafe or a tea party depending on the game being played that afternoon.
Inside are a toy sink, a stove, a cordless phone, and an assortment of other accessories to work with. Flowerpot holders on the exterior give young gardeners somewhere to put their pots. The pieces arrive pre-cut, pre-stained, and pre-drilled, so putting it together is mostly a matter of working through the sequence in order.

column3:
Cedar construction finished in white with black trim gives the Sweetwater Playhouse the look of a cottage. Backyard Discovery fits it with large windows that keep the interior bright and let a breeze move through on warm days. Decorative flowerpot holders sit on the outside for children who want to plant something, and a working half door gives them an entrance of their own. A snack bar window is where most of the pretend cafe and tea party business ends up happening.
Inside there is a toy sink, a stove, a cordless phone, and a range of other play accessories. Pieces arrive pre-cut, pre-stained, and pre-drilled, so putting it together is a matter of following the sequence rather than cutting and finishing lumber yourself.

column3:
Tacoma Falls stacks two separate play spaces into one structure. The upper clubhouse has windows, a wooden roof, and a built-in chalkboard, with a crow's nest lookout and toy telescope above it. Two slides run down from that level, an enclosed spiral tube slide that twists on the way and a wave slide for a faster straight shot. A rock wall and a step ladder give kids two ways back up.
The lower playhouse has its own full front door and a play kitchen behind it, with a toy sink, a cookware set, a dinner bell, and battery-powered accessories. Two belt swings and a web disc swing hang alongside the structure.
Backyard Discovery builds the set from natural cedar and ships it ready to assemble, with guided instructions in the BILT app. It carries a 5-year warranty.

The Tanglewood works on two levels. Up top is a clubhouse with a peak roof and a mini porch, reached by a rock wall ladder whose six holds double as steps for kids who want the simpler route. An 8-foot wave slide runs back down to the ground from there.
Beneath the clubhouse sits a playhouse with white-trimmed windows and a snack bar window under a small wooden roof, with built-in wooden bench seating underneath it for snack breaks and quieter play. Two classic belt swings and a trapeze bar give three places to swing at once.
The set is built from cedar and arrives ready to assemble, with step-by-step guidance in the BILT app. Backyard Discovery covers it with a 5-year warranty.

column3:
A connecting bridge is what sets the Timber Crossing apart, running out from the elevated play area to a rock wall attached at its far end. The upper clubhouse has a wood roof, a balcony, and wide windows that keep the space open and light. A second climbing wall with a rope assist goes up the back of the clubhouse, and a flat wide step ladder gives younger kids a straightforward way up.
Coming down is an 8-foot wave slide. Swinging happens on two belt swings, a trapeze bar, and a large web disc swing wide enough for more than one child.
The wood is natural cedar in a light brown stain with black trim. Backyard Discovery ships the set ready to assemble with guided instructions in the BILT app and backs it with a 5-year warranty.

column2: Timber Rock Outdoor Argentine Grill Cook Station
column3:
Argentine grilling over an open fire is what the Timber Rock cook station is built around. Adjustable stainless steel grates and S-hooks let you raise, lower, or hang different cuts depending on how fast you want them to cook, and the open-fire design leaves a large working surface for slow roasting. Firebrick and ceramic-lined walls behind powder-coated steel hold heat steady through a long cook.
The station is solid cedar and powder-coated galvanized steel, chosen to resist rust, dents, and corrosion outdoors. Quartz countertops give you room to prep and plate, and drawers plus open storage below keep wood, tools, and accessories in order. The cantilever roof uses Pro-Tect tested construction rated to withstand up to 2,150 pounds of snow load and 100 mph winds.
It ships ready to assemble with step-by-step BILT instructions.

column3:
Wide windows on the Timberlake let daylight and moving air into an interior with room for more than one child at a time. Backyard Discovery finishes the outside with flowerpot holders and a working half door, and a snack bar window opens onto a counter for serving up whatever is on the pretend menu.
Inside there is a play sink, a toy stove, and a cordless phone. The playhouse is built from durable cedar, sized for solo play or a group of friends, and it arrives ready to assemble.

column3:
Shade is designed into the Tucson at both levels. The raised deck sits under a brightly colored canopy roof, and the play space beneath the deck stays in the shadow of it, with a snack bar window and built-in bench seating along one side for juice breaks or drawing. That lower area can be filled with sand to make a sandbox, though sand is not included.
Kids reach the deck by a rock wall with six holds that also works as a ladder, then take the 8-foot wave slide back down. Two belt swings and a trapeze bar round out the active play.
The cedar carries a burnt sienna finish, and pieces come pre-cut, pre-drilled, and pre-stained with guided setup in the BILT app. Backyard Discovery covers the set for 5 years.

column2: Tuscany Corner Pergola with Conversation Seating - Privacy Panels
column3:
The Tuscany is a corner pergola with the seating built into it, so it sits along the edge of a patio instead of occupying the middle of it. Two oversized sofas anchor to a powder-coated steel base that ties directly into the cedar posts, which means the furniture and the frame hold together as one piece rather than sitting loose underneath. A fixed Meranti wood table goes between them, and the arrangement seats four to six.
Framing is cedar throughout, substantial enough to give the structure real weight on a patio, and cedar holds up to year-round weather without rotting or decaying. The slat roof filters direct sun into shade, while composite privacy panels along the back walls screen the seating from neighbors and leave the open sides uncovered.
It comes ready to assemble, with a 5-year warranty covering every component.

column3:
Verona is a corner pergola, shaped to tuck into the angle of a yard, patio, or deck and turn that corner into a defined, sheltered spot. Construction is 100 percent cedar and heavy-duty rather than lightweight, with composite panels that supply both shade and seclusion. The finish is a light brown stain.
Because it encloses a corner rather than standing free in the open, it suits a fire pit enclosure or a quiet reading nook equally well, and it works poolside or in a garden corner.
Materials arrive pre-cut, pre-drilled, and pre-stained, and the BILT app walks through assembly step by step. Backyard Discovery backs the pergola with a 5-year warranty.

column3:
Several routes lead up to the Voyager's clubhouse. Kids can swing across the monkey bars, scale a rock wall with 12 holds, or take the flat-step ladder with handles. The clubhouse at the top is large, with a covered entryway, a balcony, windows, and a peaked roof, and a 10-foot wave slide brings riders back to the ground.
The space under the deck is left open on purpose. It holds sand for digging, takes a blanket for a picnic, or becomes a play cafe through the attached snack bar window. Two belt swings and a trapeze hang alongside.
Construction is all cedar, which naturally resists warping, decay, and insect damage. The set is designed for up to 11 kids and engineered to meet or exceed ASTM F1148-22, for residential use only. The pre-stained warm light brown finish varies in saturation and color. It ships ready to assemble with guided BILT instructions and a 5-year warranty.

A ten-foot wave slide from Backyard Discovery, the wave being the dip and rise along its length rather than a straight drop.
It is sold on its own, which makes it a replacement for a slide that has worn out or a way to add one to a structure that can take it. No frame or hardware for building a tower comes with it. Home24Care lists it alongside the gray and yellow versions of the same slide.

Bay windows give the Whispering Point's upper clubhouse more character than a plain walled box, and a crow's nest lookout above it comes with a toy telescope. The play kitchen on the lower level is well stocked, with a toy stovetop, a sink and faucet, a battery-powered blender, and a cookware set.
Climbing routes include a rock wall and a rope climbing wall, with a step ladder for children not ready for either. Two belt swings and a web disc swing handle the swinging, and an 8-foot wave slide runs down from the clubhouse.
The structure is cedar. It arrives ready to assemble with guided instructions in the BILT app, and Backyard Discovery covers it with a 5-year warranty.

column3:
An octagonal play space sits beneath the Woodland's clubhouse, with a half door opening onto a snack bar serving station and three built-in seats around it. The clubhouse above has a peak roof and diamond-shaped peepholes, which is where the forest cottage look comes from.
Two ways lead up to it, a rock wall for kids who want the climb and a flat step ladder for those who do not. The 10-foot wave slide is the way back down. Two classic belt swings and a trapeze bar sit alongside for swinging and gymnastic-style play.
Cedar gives the set its strength and its weather resistance. It ships ready to assemble with guided instructions in the BILT app from Backyard Discovery.

column3:
A tunnel runs between play levels on the Woodridge Elite, ending at a crow's nest lookout. The clubhouse it connects has a wooden roof and windows, and a wrap-around porch breaks the upper level into several distinct areas rather than one flat platform, including a lean-to that opens onto the 10-foot wave slide.
The rock wall is extra tall and doubles as a ladder, so climbing up and walking up are both options. Down below, the lower play area has a shaded wooden deck with a built-in bench, plus adjacent ground suited to a sandbox. Two classic belt swings and a trapeze bar hang alongside.
The set is built from naturally durable cedar. It arrives ready to assemble, with guided instructions in the Backyard Discovery BILT app.
